description.text: Filippo Baldinucci was born into a prominent Florentine merchant family and entered the service of Cardinal Leopoldo de' Medici in 1664 as a bookkeeper. After the Cardinal's death he became the de facto curator of the Grand Ducal collections, where he reorganised and expanded the Medici holdings, applying new ideas of organisation and completeness that laid the groundwork for the modern Uffizi museum.

Baldinucci is best known for his biographical dictionary of artists, published in 1681 and continued after his death, which extended Vasari's approach to include artists from all of Italy and beyond. His Vocabolario (1681) was the first dictionary of artistic terms, and he also recorded the first Italian mention of Rembrandt's prints. A devout Jesuit, he completed Ignatius of Loyola's Spiritual Exercises before marriage, and his sons pursued ecclesiastical careers, one of whom was later beatified.

curiosities.text: Baldinucci expanded Vasari's biographies by including French and Flemish artists that Vasari had omitted.
He pioneered the practice of distinguishing between the hands of different painters, a new idea that laid the foundation for modern connoisseurship.
Baldinucci's son later wrote the first biography of him.
